diagnosis: The gate failed because 2 of 4 rollouts failed content checks C6 and C7 respectively, which are gated by facts PF1 and PF3. In every rollout all four facts (PF1, PF2, PF3, PF4) were revealed and cited in justification_fact_ids, so the failure is not disclosure or telepathy. Rollout 1 failed C6 (linked to PF1) and rollout 3 failed C7 (linked to PF3) despite PF1 and PF3 being both revealed and cited in those rollouts — this is an encoding mismatch. The settlement wording for the open_source_action field in rollout 1 ('module M-17 must be replaced with a compliant alternative before external customer access') likely did not match C6's expected encoding, and the permitted_intended_use_description in rollout 3 ('administrative workflow tool only') was too terse versus rollouts 0 and 2 which included the full 'no diagnostic claims or automated clinical triage' language that C7 apparently requires. No rollouts hit the turn cap; all settled within 6-11 turns.

C6.why: The production build would otherwise remain on the standard proprietary path, while PF1 changes the required software action to identifying the AGPL issue and replacing exactly module M-17 before external customer access, with launch withheld until that control is complete.

C7.why: The standard launch wording would continue to describe automated clinical triage or diagnostic functionality, while PF3 changes the permitted description to the exact phrase administrative workflow tool only and requires prohibited diagnostic and triage language to be removed.
